stories.title: Cyanogen co-founder launches Kora, a Linux-based desktop OS for AI power users
stories.summary: The co-founder of Cyanogen is launching Kora, a free Linux-based alternative to Windows built for power users who rely heavily on local AI models and agents.
stories.more: Kora is positioned as a next-generation alternative to both Windows and macOS, aimed specifically at power users who run local AI models. TechCrunch frames it as a parallel to the founder's earlier challenge to Android with Cyanogen, this time targeting Windows for the AI era. Wired describes it as built for 'AI nerds' who run models locally rather than relying on cloud AI. The coverage does not specify a release date, system requirements, or which local AI frameworks Kora supports out of the box.

items.title: After challenging Google’s Android with Cyanogen, its co-founder takes aim at Windows for AI era
items.excerpt: Kora is set to launch as a free-to-use alternative to Windows, targeting users who rely heavily on AI models and agents.

items.title: This New Linux-Based Desktop Operating System Is Built for AI Nerds
items.excerpt: Built by Cyanogen’s cofounder, Kora is a next-gen alternative to Windows and macOS built for power users running local AI models.

stories.title: Meta's AI agent Muse comes to Apple Watch and Wear OS
stories.summary: Meta brought its AI agent Muse to Apple Watch and Android's Wear OS, letting users interact with it through voice calls, text messages, or dictation.
stories.more: The expansion lets Muse users reach the assistant directly from their wrist rather than only through a phone app. TechCrunch lists three interaction methods now supported on wearables: voice calls, text messages, and dictation. The report does not specify which Wear OS versions or Apple Watch models are supported, nor whether the feature is rolling out globally at launch.

items.title: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
items.excerpt: Users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation on their Apple Watch.

stories.title: Adobe adds easier object-removal tools to Photoshop, Lightroom, and Premiere
stories.summary: At Adobe Max, Adobe announced new generative AI features that automatically remove unwanted objects, blemishes, and distractions across Photoshop, Premiere, and Lightroom.
stories.more: The features were announced among Adobe's Creative Cloud and Firefly AI platform updates at its Max 2026 event. They aim to make removing unwanted elements, such as blemishes or background distractions, faster and less complicated for editors. Premiere, Photoshop, and Lightroom are all named as receiving removal-related capabilities. The coverage does not specify exact release dates or whether the features are available to all subscription tiers.

stories.title: Spotify's AI DJ adds new voices and a less-chatty mode
stories.summary: Spotify Premium users can now customize their AI DJ with new voice personalities or switch to a mode with less commentary between songs.
stories.more: The update is aimed at Spotify Premium subscribers specifically. It adds multiple new voice options, each described as having a distinct personality, for the AI DJ feature. Users can also opt for reduced commentary between tracks if they prefer less talking. TechCrunch's report does not specify exactly how many new voices were added or whether the feature is rolling out to all markets at once.

items.title: Spotify’s AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter
items.excerpt: Spotify Premium users can now customize their AI DJ with new voices with different personalities, or turn off the commentary between songs.

stories.title: Ring unveils AI-powered indoor drone camera, shipping January 2027 for $249.99
stories.summary: Ring is finally shipping an indoor flying drone camera, the Ring Drone Cam, priced at $249.99 and set to arrive January 27, 2027, nearly six years after it was first announced.
stories.more: Ring founder Jamie Siminoff announced the Ring Drone Cam's price and ship date at a launch event in New York City. The device is described as an indoor flying camera, and The Verge notes the company has promised a product like this for almost six years without shipping one. The report is a hands-on preview rather than a full review and notes skepticism about whether it will actually ship on schedule this time. No additional technical specifications were included in the excerpt.

stories.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for Healthcare to unify clinical data
stories.summary: Google Cloud launched Gemini for Healthcare, a product meant to unify clinical data and automate healthcare workflows in order to reduce administrative burnout.
stories.more: Gemini for Healthcare is positioned by Google Cloud as a way to bring together clinical data that is normally scattered across systems. The product automates workflows, which Google frames as a way to reduce administrative burnout among healthcare staff. The announcement did not detail which health systems or partners are adopting it, or when it becomes generally available. No pricing information was included in the source excerpt.

items.excerpt: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare to unify clinical data and automate workflows. Reduce administrative burnout. See how it works.

stories.title: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow with $70-$78 share price, up to $1.4 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic confirmed its IPO roadshow, pricing shares at $70 to $78 and targeting a valuation as high as $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, among the biggest IPOs ever.
stories.more: Anthropic's IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share implies a valuation of up to $1.404 trillion on a fully diluted basis, according to TechCrunch. The Verge reports the same price range and notes the IPO could rank among the biggest ever, even though it falls short of some earlier expectations reported by the New York Times and Wall Street Journal. The Decoder separately describes the roadshow as targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion, alongside a public offering of up to $64.4 billion and a further $26 billion raised through a private placement with anchor investors including Google, Nvidia, and Microsoft. The sources do not fully reconcile these two valuation figures. Coverage notes the roadshow comes as investors have grown more skeptical of AI investments generally.

stories.title: Google and Adobe partner to bring Adobe's creative tools into Google apps
stories.summary: Google and Adobe announced a partnership integrating Adobe's creative and productivity tools into everyday Google apps, letting users edit PDFs in Drive and access Adobe AI inside Gemini.
stories.more: The partnership brings Adobe's creative and productivity tools closer to Google's everyday apps rather than keeping them siloed in Adobe's own products. One concrete feature mentioned is the ability to edit PDFs directly inside Google Drive. The integration also brings Adobe AI capabilities into Gemini. The announcement did not specify a rollout timeline or which Adobe tools beyond PDF editing are included.

stories.title: OpenAI Academy runs free ChatGPT workshops for caregivers in five US cities
stories.summary: OpenAI is running free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops for caregivers in five U.S. cities through OpenAI Academy, aiming to help them build practical AI skills for everyday caregiving.
stories.more: The workshops are organized under OpenAI Academy, the company's education initiative, and target caregivers specifically rather than the general public. They are free and hands-on, and are being held in five U.S. cities. The stated goal is to help caregivers build practical AI skills they can use in everyday life. No further details on curriculum, dates, or which cities are included in the source excerpt.

items.title: Helping caregivers use AI in everyday life

Google describes Carbon as its strongest model to date, positioning it as competitive with the best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI. The release introduces an agent 'swarm' feature, though the available coverage does not detail how it works. DeepMind's own announcement of the model's availability did not add further specifics beyond confirming the release.

stories.title: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41% of real freelance jobs, up from 2.5% a year ago
stories.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completed 41.3% of real freelance jobs at professional quality on the Remote Labor Index, more than double the next-best systems, up from 2.5% a year earlier.
stories.more: The Decoder reports Fable 5.2 outperforms the next-best systems, named as Opus 5.5 and GPT 6 Astra, on the Remote Labor Index benchmark of real freelance jobs. The jump from roughly 2.5 percent a year ago to 41.3 percent today represents a large year-over-year gain on this measure. The report notes that areas like product design and animation remain comparative weak spots for the model. No details were given on the size or composition of the job set used in the index.

stories.title: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code verifies Signal's encryption with 3M lines of Lean proofs
stories.summary: DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a system whose agents wrote three million lines of formal proofs in the Lean language to verify the correctness of Signal's core encryption.
stories.more: DeepMind calls AlphaProof Code a system for verifying complex software at depth, extending its AlphaProof line of work into code and proof verification. In its first showcased application, AlphaProof Code agents produced roughly three million lines of proofs written in the Lean proof assistant language. Those proofs were used to verify Signal's core encryption implementation. The announcement does not specify what, if anything, the proofs found, or when the tool will be made more broadly available.

items.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
items.excerpt: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.

stories.title: New benchmark Longtail-SWE tests coding models on 13 underrepresented languages
stories.summary: Researchers introduced Longtail-SWE, a 202-task benchmark of issue-resolution problems across 13 programming languages with little existing benchmark coverage, including Clojure, Haskell, and Swift.
stories.more: Longtail-SWE contains 202 issue-resolution tasks spanning 13 languages that existing repository-level benchmarks cover poorly: Clojure, Dart, Elixir, Erlang, F#, Haskell, Julia, Kotlin, Lua, OCaml, R, Scala, and Swift. The paper argues that candidate tasks for these ecosystems are scarce and are often filtered out for having ambiguous descriptions or defective tests, discarding potentially valuable engineering problems. It is unclear from the available excerpt how current coding models perform on the new benchmark.

stories.title: Adobe opens Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly to AI agents with a new MCP
stories.summary: At Adobe Max, Adobe said it is letting third-party AI agents access and change its creative apps through a new MCP, while adding a Firefly prototype-builder tool aimed at Figma.
stories.more: Adobe used its Max conference in Miami to lay out a broader agentic AI strategy, framing chatbots and AI agents as potential design assistants that could automate creative workflows or repetitive tasks. Among the announcements, Adobe is allowing preferred third-party AI agents to access and change its Creative Cloud apps through a new MCP integration. Separately, Adobe is adding a prototype-builder tool to Firefly that TechCrunch frames as a challenge to Figma. The coverage does not list every feature announced or specify a rollout timeline for the agent access.

stories.title: eBay appears to block third-party AI agents like Meta's Muse from the platform
stories.summary: eBay seems to have cut off access for third-party AI shopping agents, including Meta's Muse, in what The Verge calls the latest setback in the race to build agentic shopping tools.
stories.more: A reader told The Verge that for several weeks they had used a Meta Muse agent to browse and curate a daily digest of items for sale on platforms including eBay, such as watches. That access now appears to have been shut off. The Verge frames this as part of a broader pattern of platforms putting up barriers to AI agents browsing on their behalf. The report does not state whether eBay issued an official statement on the change or how it is technically blocking agent traffic.

stories.title: Google adds two new specialized TPUs for confidential training and more memory
stories.summary: Google broadened its AI chip portfolio with two new tensor processing units aimed at confidential model training and workloads that need greater memory capacity.
stories.more: The new TPUs extend Google's existing chip lineup to cover more specialized use cases. One focus area is confidential model training, implying added security or isolation features for training workloads. The other addresses use cases that need more memory capacity than prior TPU generations offered. TechCrunch's report does not include specific performance benchmarks, pricing, or availability dates for the new chips.

items.excerpt: Google's new tensor processing units (TPUs) broaden its chip portfolio to more use cases: confidential model training and more memory capacity.

stories.title: Ukraine's fiber-optic drone supply gets squeezed by AI data center demand
stories.summary: Ukraine is competing with Russia and with AI data centers for China's optical fiber supply, Ars Technica reports, as demand for fiber used in both drones and AI infrastructure rises.
stories.more: The report ties Ukraine's fiber-optic drone production to a global supply chain for optical fiber that AI data center buildouts are also drawing on. Ars Technica frames this as a competition for supply involving Ukraine, Russia, and data center demand, with China named as a key source of the fiber. The excerpt does not quantify how much AI-related demand has affected fiber prices or availability for drone manufacturers, nor does it specify a timeframe over which this competition has intensified.

stories.title: Hugging Face exec warns cyberattacks could make open-source AI less open
stories.summary: Hugging Face's Irene Solaiman warned that rising cyberattacks on open AI platforms could push the industry toward tighter security restrictions that reduce the openness developers rely on.
stories.more: The warning comes from Irene Solaiman, identified as a Hugging Face executive, in comments reported by TechCrunch. The concern is that growing cyberattacks targeting open AI platforms could force operators to adopt tighter security restrictions. Those restrictions could in turn reduce the accessibility that makes open-source AI communities valuable to developers worldwide. The report does not cite a specific recent attack or name which platforms would be affected.

items.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open-source AI a little less open, Hugging Face exec warns
items.excerpt: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warns that growing cyberattacks on open AI platforms could force tighter security restrictions, threatening the accessibility that makes open-source communities valuable to developers worldwide.

stories.title: Eight countries and major AI labs sign Paris declaration on shutdown mechanisms
stories.summary: Eight countries and AI labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Mistral AI signed a Paris declaration committing to shutdown mechanisms, independent audits, and risk disclosure, with no binding sanctions.
stories.more: The agreement, called the Paris Call for AI Safety and Security, was signed at an initiative led by Emmanuel Macron. Signatories include eight countries along with AI companies OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Mistral AI. The companies commit to building shutdown mechanisms into their systems, submitting to independent audits, and disclosing known risks. The Decoder notes the declaration lacks binding sanctions or deadlines, meaning compliance is not legally enforced.

stories.title: DeepMind unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open 'ASIMOV-jailbreak' safety benchmark
stories.summary: DeepMind revealed Gemini Robotics 2.5, a robotics model up to twice as successful at some tasks as before, alongside a new open safety benchmark called ASIMOV-jailbreak.
stories.more: Ars Technica reports the new model, Gemini Robotics 2.5, achieves up to twice the success rate of its predecessor on some tasks, though the report does not specify which tasks or by how much across the board. Alongside the model, DeepMind released an open safety benchmark named ASIMOV-jailbreak. The benchmark's exact methodology and what it measures are not detailed in the available excerpt. It is unclear from the report how the model and benchmark relate to each other beyond being announced together.
